topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: Defocused reflectors introduce increased spillover losses, leading to higher multipath interference and reduced SNR. This necessitates increased power levels for equivalent SNR, impacting channel capacity.  Conventional designs can achieve better SNR with less power due to narrower beam patterns, offering a trade-off between performance and complexity.
reference_context: Defocused reflector antennas offer broader beam patterns, potentially increasing bandwidth efficiency but at the expense of gain and reduced SNR.
